subtitle: Spain, France, and England head the 2026 World Cup market as the top European sides with elite squad depth and strong recent form heading into the expanded 48-team tournament. Spain’s Euro 2024 title and attacking options around Lamine Yamal and Rodri underpin their narrow lead, while France’s blend of experience and youth keeps them within a fraction. England’s perfect qualifying record under Thomas Tuchel supports their position ahead of Brazil and defending champions Argentina. The tight clustering among the leading contenders reflects comparable talent pools, favorable group draws for several favorites, and the inherent unpredictability of knockout stages where one injury or off day can shift outcomes.
